observation.visible_scene: Elevated daytime view of a sandy beach and open ocean under a clear blue sky, filmed from a pier/boardwalk structure (Ocean City, MD per overlay). A large curved shadow (pier) fills the lower-left; rectangular structure shadows and a railing line the right edge. Scattered small figures/objects sit on the sand. Fixed text overlays appear top-right ('Filmed by Oleg Kapplun / Ocean City, MD') and bottom-left ('Music by Puddle of Infinity'). A faint point sits high in the sky. The horizon and framing stay essentially constant throughout.
visible_changes: Ocean surf is an ongoing process: white foam lines along the shoreline continuously advance, break, and retreat, shifting shape and position from frame to frame (e.g., the breaking line near center-left and the foam bands near the waterline change configuration across the clip).

A bird with spread wings briefly crosses the right portion of the view over the water/beach boundary around t=0.067s (visible in frame 2, absent in frames 1 and 3); a small dark shape also appears at the far-right horizon edge around t=0.33s.
The overall camera position and background layout (horizon, shadow shapes, pier edge, text overlays) remain static; no clear pan or zoom is supported.
The small figures on the beach remain in roughly the same positions; no definite locomotion is confirmed.
outside_clip_unknowns: Where the bird entered from and where it exits after leaving the frame.
Whether the faint sky point is the moon or another object.
Any beachgoer motion occurring between the sampled frames or outside this segment.
uncertain_details: Possible very slight camera drift vs. a perfectly static shot (background evidence is too stable to confirm motion).
Exact movement of individual beach figures (dots too small to track reliably).
Whether the right-edge dark shape in frame 6 is a second bird or a transient artifact.

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
